verdict.root_cause: In _strip_docstring (src/haute/_ast_helpers.py:203-231) the single-line fast-path at :221 requires `stripped.endswith(opening_quote)`. With a trailing comment the line ends with the comment text, so execution falls to the `else` at :224-226 setting in_docstring=True. The close test at :215 (`if opening_quote in stripped`) then looks for a LATER line containing `"""`; the only such line was the already-consumed opener, so every remaining body line hits `continue` (:218) and is never appended, yielding []. The same opener-as-docstring assumption misfires when the first statement is a triple-quoted BinOp (`"""a""" + foo`), which ast does NOT treat as a docstring. No upstream guard prevents this: _extract_function_bodies (:269-274) slices raw source lines verbatim (docstring line included, comment preserved), and the parser only requires valid Python — which all these cases are.

verdict.recommended_fix: The finding's specific claim (fallback_parse causing preserved-block data loss on the next save) is refuted: the GUI save round-trip never carries preserved_blocks at all, so the loss is path-independent and not attributable to the fallback parser. Two separable points: (1) For consistency/correctness, fallback_parse (src/haute/_parser_regex.py:759-767) SHOULD still call _extract_preserved_blocks(source) and pass preserved_blocks=... to PipelineGraph, mirroring parser.py:165-176 — _extract_preserved_blocks is text-only and works on broken source. This is a benign cleanup (low), not a data-loss fix, because no production codepath round-trips a parser-produced graph through codegen. (2) The genuine (pre-existing, separate) data-loss-on-save of preserved blocks lives in the frontend/save contract: the frontend PipelineGraph/GraphPayload types and handleSave drop preserved_blocks, so any GUI save regenerates the file without them. Fixing THAT requires either threading preserved_blocks through the load->store->save payload, or having the backend save service re-read existing preserved blocks from the on-disk file before codegen. That is the issue to file; V052 as written misdiagnoses the location and cause.
